hypotheses.hypothesis: The memcmp function is used to compare the challenge hash values c and c2, which are secret-derived. The memcmp function returns early on the first mismatch, leaking the secret value byte-by-byte.
hypotheses.trigger_condition: Any two different values of c and c2
hypotheses.test_vector_hint: Run 10000 iterations with different values of c and c2, measure delta.
hypotheses.evidence: mean_A=24.898ns vs mean_B=24.861ns, t_statistic=0.2687, significant=false across 50000 runs.
hypotheses.next_test_hint: Retest with higher sample counts (100000+) and refined conditions to detect subtle timing variations.

feedback.note: LEAK-1 memcmp ML-DSA-44 challenge comparison oracle. Cond-A: memcmp(c,c2,32) where c==c2 (full 32-byte scan). Cond-B: memcmp(c,c2,32) where c[0]!=c2[0] (exits at byte 0). Injection: mld_ct_memcmp replaced with memcmp in mld_sign_verify_internal. Signal: early-exit timing of non-constant-time challenge comparison.
